candidates.exact_span: As used in this document, references to State water quality standards and/or rules, regulations and/or management plans may mean the State of New Mexico and/or Tribal or both.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The permissive 'may mean' and 'and/or Tribal or both' leave unclear whether NM state, Tribal, or both regulatory frameworks govern cited standards, rules, and management plans. Different readings would change which numeric limits are treated as applicable (A), which monitoring requirements are in force (B), and how missing or conditional monitoring evidence is classified when the governing standard set is unresolved (C).

This defines WQBELs as water quality-based effluent limitations. How downstream permit text referencing WQBELs is mapped to this category affects whether a cited value is treated as an enforceable numeric discharge limit versus report-only or non-comparable monitoring.

WLA identifies limits derived through waste-load allocation. Interpreting whether a cited allocation is an applicable enforceable numeric limit, and how it relates to other limit types, can change which limit is selected for compliance comparison.

WET defines whole effluent toxicity testing. Whether permit provisions labeled WET are read as imposing enforceable numeric toxicity limits (A) and/or distinct toxicity monitoring obligations (B) depends on applying this defined term to those provisions.
